text: Initial structural check: Q is a strategic game with separate private allocations \(x_n\), price bids \(p_n\), and exact proximal best responses (Q lines 141-194, 429-490). P is cooperative minimization of one shared decision \(x\) by consensus and projected zeroth-order gradient updates (P lines 274-290, 374-490). Thus P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s algorithm cannot simply be inserted into Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s VS-PBR inner loop. P supplies a CVaR value/gradient oracle and an error bound, but Q needs a new inexact best-response argument. I am checking whether Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s payment proof is valuation-agnostic under concave risk utility, and what exact error schedule can restore convergence.

First structural check: Q, lines 110-139, assumes only expected valuation \(V_n=\mathbb E\psi_n\) is twice differentiable and \(\alpha\)-strongly concave; P, lines 317-490, supplies an empirical-CVaR one-point gradient inside projected consensus gradient descent for a common decision \(x\), not a best-response oracle for Q\x27s coupled game. Thus the scan\x27s direct plug-in is unsupported. I am testing a narrower route: define risk-adjusted valuation \(R_n(x_n)=-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}[-\psi_n(x_n,\xi_n)]\), check when Q\x27s mechanism still works, then quantify what P\x27s finite-sample/smoothing bias implies for equilibrium accuracy.

Concrete curvature counterexample (Q lines 119-136; P lines 327-340, 493-515). Let \(x\in[0,1]\), and loss \(J(x,\xi)\) equal \(10\) or \(x^2\), each with probability \(1/2\). Every sample loss is convex, bounded, Lipschitz; normalized expected valuation \(V(x)=-\mathbb E J(x,\xi)+\mathbb E J(0,\xi)=-x^2/2\) is strongly concave, satisfying Q. But for P tail mass \(\beta=1/2\), normalized risk valuation \(R(x)=-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(J(x,\xi))+\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(J(0,\xi))=0\) throughout \([0,1]\). Hence expectation curvature does not transfer to CVaR. In Q explicit payment (40), at any \(p_n=0\) and \(\sum_n x_n\le c\), each agent has zero allocation marginal and nonnegative price marginal, so every such profile is a NE for these flat risk valuations: uniqueness is lost. A restoration theorem needs strong concavity of risk valuation itself, or common samplewise strong convexity of losses, and a nonsmooth monotonicity proof.

Core conditional result: for loss \(J_n=-\psi_n\), define \(R_n(x)=-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}(J_n(x,\xi_n))\). If every sample \(J_n(\cdot,\xi_n)\) is uniformly \(m\)-strongly convex, then \(J_n(x,\xi_n)-m\|x\|^2/2\) is convex and CVaR cash translation gives \(C_n(x)-m\|x\|^2/2=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}(J_n(x,\xi_n)-m\|x\|^2/2)\), so \(R_n\) is \(m\)-strongly concave even if kinked. Deterministic tax cash translation gives \(-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}[-\psi_n(x,\xi_n)+t_n(s)]=R_n(x)-t_n(s)\); hence Q\x27s equilibrium/KKT and budget algebra can apply to the risk-adjusted social objective with subgradients, provided its other conditions and suitable constraint qualification hold. IR is relative to \(R_n(0)\), or normalize \(R_n(0)=0\). Q: Assumption valuation_function_assumption and Theorem nash_implementation_theorem (lines 126-139, 240-322); P: CVaR representation and convexity lemma (lines 327-341, 505-515).

Q\x27s expected-value curvature does not transfer to CVaR. Example on \(x\in[0,1]\): equiprobable convex losses \(J(x,\xi_1)=0\), \(J(x,\xi_2)=x^2-1\). Then \(\mathbb E J=(x^2-1)/2\) is strongly convex, while \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(J)=\max\{0,x^2-1\}=0\) throughout \([0,1]\). Thus expected satisfaction \(\mathbb E[-J]\) is strongly concave yet risk-adjusted satisfaction \(-\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(J)\) is flat. Shifting each sample by a deterministic constant normalizes the outside value without restoring curvature. So Q\x27s P1 LMI cannot simply retain its \(\alpha\) after a CVaR swap. P assumes per-sample convexity, but not uniform strong convexity (Assumption convex, lines 501-503).

Sharper joint question: how accurately can finite-batch empirical-CVaR learning implement Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s true risk-welfare NE, including ex-post IR? P lines 868-960 proves fixed batch converges to the optimizer of expected smoothed empirical CVaR, not true CVaR; P lines 1279-1330 bounds CVaR value bias by \(O(1/(\beta\sqrt{s}))\). Explicit even with preserved curvature: let each agent have \(x\in[0,1]\), ample capacity \(c=N\), and equiprobable sample losses \(J(x,\xi)=x^2/2-3x/4+\xi x\), \(\xi\in\{0,1\}\), at tail mass \(\beta=1/2\). True loss CVaR is \(x^2/2+x/4\), uniquely minimized at \(x=0\); but batch size \(s=1\) gives expected empirical CVaR \(x^2/2-x/4\), minimized at \(x=1/4\). Both are strongly convex. For Q payment (40), \(p=0\) under slack capacity, so the surrogate NE allocates \(1/4\) to each agent yet true risk utility is \(-3/32<0\) per agent and opt-out utility is \(0\): exact Nash implementation and individual rationality fail for the learning limit, even though the ideal risk mechanism has them. Fixed smoothing of this quadratic does not change its interior minimizer. This is a falsifiable target for an approximate implementation theorem plus a schedule of \(s_k\) and \(\delta_k\) restoring exactness.

Alternative sharper target from P appendix (lines 1280-1287): \(\sum_n\operatorname{CVaR}_\beta(J_n)\) generally differs from \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\beta(\sum_nJ_n)\), the system tail risk. Q\x27s separable social welfare and deterministic cash-translated taxes naturally implement the former, not necessarily the latter. Explicit 2-agent counterexample: \(x_1+x_2\le1\), \(x_n\ge0\), equally likely mutually exclusive scenarios \((Z_1,Z_2)=(1,0),(0,1)\), and \(J_1=2x_1Z_1+q x_1^2-Bx_1\), \(J_2=x_2Z_2+q x_2^2-Bx_2\), with \(0<q<1/2\), \(B>2+2q\). Each loss is uniformly strongly convex and satisfies P\x27s bounded/convex assumptions on \([0,1]\). At \(\beta=1/2\), sum of local CVaRs is \(2x_1+x_2+q(x_1^2+x_2^2)-B(x_1+x_2)\), uniquely minimized at \((0,1)\); CVaR of aggregate loss is \(\max\{2x_1,x_2\}+q(x_1^2+x_2^2)-B(x_1+x_2)\), uniquely minimized at \((1/3,2/3)\). This survives the curvature repair. So one must state the welfare semantics and perhaps design scenario-contingent risk sharing if targeting system CVaR; local-CVaR implementation alone can miss diversification.

Two further limits on the scan\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s literal transplant. P requires an origin-centered ball \(r\mathbb B\subseteq\mathcal X\) and shrinks it before querying \(x+\delta u\) (P lines 317-325, 463-489); Q insists \(\mathcal X_n\subset\mathbb R_{\ge0}^K\) (Q lines 105-123), so that ball condition is impossible for any \(r>0\), and Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s EV flow equalities can leave no ambient interior (Q lines 617-660). A feasible risk oracle needs relative-interior perturbations or an extension of the loss outside feasible allocations. Also P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s fixed-batch last-iterate theorem concerns its cooperative projected descent, not Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s strategic game; my explicit surrogate-NE example describes the target of such a transplanted oracle, not a proved limit of Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s VS-PBR.

Correction to #6: I used \(\text{ex-post IR}\) loosely. The computed failure is individual rationality under the true CVaR valuation, i.e. \(R_n(1/4)-t_n=-3/32<R_n(0)=0\), not a claim about every realized sample payoff. P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s one-point method also cannot be applied literally on \([0,1]\) under its origin-ball hypothesis (#8); the example concerns the fixed-batch expected empirical-CVaR objective that its oracle targets. Ada\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s #7 diversification example checks out: with \(x_1+x_2=1\), separable-risk derivative at \(x_1=0\) is \(1-2q>0\), while system-risk max switches at \(x_1=1/3\) with left derivative negative and right derivative positive. Thus the system CVaR target differs even after strong-curvature repair. I still prioritize the fixed-batch implementation/IR question as the closest concrete joint theorem and counterexample; diversification is a separate welfare-definition question.

In the #7 example, system-CVaR regret of local-CVaR allocation is exact: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(J_1+J_2)(0,1)-\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}(J_1+J_2)(1/3,2/3)=1/3+4q/9>0\). There is a conditional constructive repair: with verifiable realized losses, scenario-contingent transfers \(t_n^{\mathrm{pool}}(x,\omega)=\frac1N\sum_mJ_m(x_m,\omega)-J_n(x_n,\omega)\) obey \(\sum_nt_n^{\mathrm{pool}}=0\) in every scenario and make each net loss \(J_n+t_n^{\mathrm{pool}}=(\sum_mJ_m)/N\), so \(\sum_n\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(J_n+t_n^{\mathrm{pool}})=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta}(\sum_mJ_m)\). This is an identity, not yet a truthful mechanism: Q keeps private satisfaction, so loss verification/reporting and combined price incentives are open. It shows why deterministic Q taxes plus individual CVaR cannot generally capture pooling.

A tractable theorem target is sensitivity of the strategic equilibrium, not reuse of P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s consensus proof. Under common samplewise curvature \(m>0\), a feasible smoothing oracle, and a Q-type LMI yielding strong monotonicity constant \(\nu>0\) for the smoothed game, let \(s_{\delta}\) and \(\widetilde s_{\delta,s}\) be true-smoothed and fixed-batch expected-empirical-smoothed NE. P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s DKW gradient bound (P lines 1279-1330, 908-945) gives uniform operator difference \(B_{\delta,s}\le\sqrt{\sum_n 2\pi d_n^2U_n^2/(\beta_n^2\delta_n^2s_n)}\). Two VI inequalities plus strong monotonicity imply \(\|\widetilde s_{\delta,s}-s_{\delta}\|\le B_{\delta,s}/\nu\). If smoothing approximates the unsmoothed payoff uniformly by \(O(\delta)\) on suitably feasible domains, compactness and unique NE give \(s_{\delta}\to s^*\) as \(\delta\to0\); thus choose \(\delta\to0\) and \(\delta_n\sqrt{s_n}\to\infty\) for asymptotic equilibrium recovery. For finite \(s,\delta\), exact true-risk IR is not robust without a positive participation margin, as #6 demonstrates. This is conditional on constructing a strategic learning algorithm and feasible oracle; neither paper proves that step.

My preferred publication line is a risk-aware strategic mechanism with an explicit learning-to-implementation guarantee: first preserve Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s ideal quadratic-tax result under direct risk-valuation strong concavity (or common samplewise loss curvature) using nonsmooth monotonicity/KKT; then quantify P\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s empirical-CVaR and smoothing distortion at the game equilibrium, and state approximate IR and budget/implementation guarantees. #6 is a decisive finite-batch failure of exact true-risk implementation/IR despite curvature; #11 gives a conditional equilibrium error bound. A genuinely new result requires a feasible zeroth-order oracle on Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s nonnegative/affine sets and a strategic algorithm convergence proof. Ada\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s #7/#10 is a distinct, validated systemic-risk avenue: deterministic local-CVaR welfare differs from CVaR of aggregate loss, and scenario transfers need verifiable losses. No prior-work novelty claim made; I did not search the web.
ready at #12

Cross-checking #11 and strengthening the participation claim: let \(\widetilde R_n=-\mathbb E_{\nu,\mathrm{batch}}\widehat C_n(x+\delta_n\nu)\) be P\x27s fixed-batch surrogate and \(R_n=-C_n\). P\x27s Lemma smoothed cvar Lipschitz (lines 505-507) and appendix DKW calculation (1290-1328) imply the deterministic uniform bound \(\sup_x|\widetilde R_n(x)-R_n(x)|\le e_n:=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\), on a domain where perturbation queries are valid. At a surrogate NE, Q\x27s IR deviation \((x_n,p_n)=(0,\tilde p)\) and nonpositive deviation tax imply \(\widetilde R_n(\widetilde x_n)-t_n(\widetilde s)\ge\widetilde R_n(0)\). Therefore true-risk participation satisfies \(R_n(\widetilde x_n)-t_n(\widetilde s)-R_n(0)\ge-2e_n\), without an equilibrium-distance estimate. A positive surrogate participation margin above \(2e_n\) suffices for exact true-risk IR; #6 shows no uniform exact IR with zero margin. This is a clean finite-sample mechanism guarantee derivable from both papers, conditional on the surrogate NE and feasible oracle.

A useful property split at an exact surrogate-game NE: if the surrogate risk valuations satisfy Q\x27s curvature/constraint hypotheses, Q\x27s P2-P3 algebra applies to that surrogate social planner, so its realized deterministic taxes still balance exactly at the surrogate NE. The finite-batch error changes which allocation is implemented and can breach true-risk IR (#6), but does not by itself cause a budget deficit at an exact surrogate NE. Off-equilibrium learning iterates need a separate balance bound. This distinguishes structural budget balance from risk-welfare and participation robustness.

Cross-check and extension of #14 (Q lines 385-405; P lines 505-507, 1290-1328): assuming every smoothing query is feasible, fixed batch size \(s_n\), tail mass \(\beta_n\), and \(|J_n|\le U_n\), set \(e_n=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\). DKW plus P smoothing gives \(\sup_x|\widetilde R_n(x)-R_n(x)|\le e_n\). At any exact NE of the surrogate game using Q taxes, each true-risk unilateral deviation improves payoff by at most \(2e_n\), since the tax cancels in the surrogate-to-true comparison. Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s P4 opt-out deviation then gives true-risk participation \(R_n(\widetilde x_n)-t_n(\widetilde s)-R_n(0)\ge-2e_n\), as Ada stated. If the same Q mechanism exactly implements the surrogate social optimum, its true separable-risk welfare gap is at most \(2\sum_ne_n\): insert surrogate welfare between true welfare at the true optimum and at the surrogate optimum. Budget balance remains exact at that surrogate NE by Q\(\!\)\(\text{\prime}\)s tax algebra, conditional on P1-P3 holding for the surrogate valuations. This is a value-level approximate implementation result, independent of the stronger and unresolved strategic learning convergence step.

My preferred publishable question, consistent with Emmy #12: under risk-adjusted \(R_n=-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}(-\psi_n)\) and enough curvature, can Q\x27s quadratic tax plus a genuinely feasible strategic zeroth-order oracle achieve quantitative true-risk Nash/IR guarantees and exact budget balance at its limiting equilibrium? The immediate theorem pieces are cash translation and samplewise curvature (#4), the fixed-batch counterexample (#6), P\x27s VI sensitivity (#11), and the direct true-risk participation bound \(-2e_n\) (#14); exact balance at a surrogate NE is structural (#15). I agree the direct scan plug-in is invalid (#1/#2/#8). My distinct systemic-risk objection (#7/#10) remains: this target implements sum of local CVaRs, which may be far from CVaR of aggregate loss, even under samplewise curvature; the exact regret example and conditional pooling-transfer identity should be retained as a separate research fork. Unresolved: oracle feasibility on Q\x27s nonnegative/affine sets, a proof for the strategic learning dynamics, possible Q LMI assumptions on price compactness, private realized-loss verification for pooling, and external novelty. I did not search the web.
